posts.text: I buy that El-Sayed's result was a pretty impressive result for the left even though he underperformed polls. But I don't buy that for Hong. It's not because she lost; both primaries were basically a tie. It's because the rest of the field was a complete mess behind her.
posts.summary: El-Sayed achieved stronger result than Hong given competitive field dynamics
posts.quote: I buy that El-Sayed's result was a pretty impressive result for the left even though he underperformed polls. But I don't buy that for Hong. It's not because she lost; both primaries were basically a tie. It's because the rest of the field was a complete mess behind her.

posts.text: *Three* of her opponents dropped out for reasons that had nothing to do with Hong's strength, including Crowley, who only re-entered the race 3 weeks ago. She almost won by forfeit, but that's much less impressive than AES holding off a sitting member of Congress with lots of $.

posts.text: There are a lot of normies. Way more than you'd think. The problem is that normies don't vote in primaries much, but normies also don't answer polls much. Pollsters kind of hope these two biases cancel out, when sometimes they don't.
